subject: lion
reasoning:
I'm planning out the lion model's skeleton structure, starting with a pelvis root joint and spine chain positioned for a standing pose facing forward.

I'm sketching the full chain hierarchy: spine through chest, neck, head, jaw, a tail chain off the pelvis, and leg chains with shoulder/elbow/wrist joints ending in paws. I'm sweeping a barrel-like body shape along the spine curve with varying radii to form the belly and chest, adjusting the spine's vertical position so the proportions match a realistic shoulder height and belly depth.

I'm now laying out the skull geometry with boxes for the skull, muzzle, and nose, placing the jaw joint for the lower jaw while keeping the upper jaw rigidly attached to the head.

Adding teeth, eyes, and ears...

Now I'm working out the hind leg chain: hip, knee, hock, and paw joints forming a bent back-leg structure, with a thicker thigh blob added near the hip for bulk and tapering sweep radii down to the paw.

I'm mirroring this across left/right sides with a sign flip on x and L/R suffixes, keeping radius arrays smoothly interpolated. For the tail, I'm laying out a drooping curved path from root to tip using several segments with shrinking radius, finishing with a darker tufted sphere at the end.

Now I'm adjusting attachment points so the spine and tail both branch from the root joint, pushing the spine start slightly further back and starting the body sweep capsule from there with a rounded rear cap near the rump.

For color, I'm setting up a countershaded palette—tan back, cream belly, dark mane tones—applying countershading to the body, legs, and head via paint on the sweep geometry, with a mottled pattern for the mane and plain gradients for smaller parts, plus sphere bulges for the shoulder/chest area.

Now I'm working out facial details: amber eye spheres with small black pupils, a brow ridge, scaled ear spheres with tan-pink inner color, a cream muzzle, and fang cones rotated to point downward for the upper teeth.

I'm also setting up the joint hierarchy — jaw joint parented to the head, head joint positioned at the end of a two-segment neck chain so the head attaches smoothly to the neck's tip.

Then I'm building the spine as a four-point catmull chain parented appropriately below the neck, with the chest widening and radius functions controlling body thickness along its length for a more natural taper.

I'm placing the hind leg joints now—hip, knee, hock, and paw positions—to form a believable rear leg bend geometry.

Setting up the leg chains with named joints, attaching front legs to the spine and hind legs to the root, and adding haunch and shoulder bulges as extra ellipsoid and sphere parts to fill out the hips and shoulders naturally.

Now I'm adding toe spheres to the paws, a tufted tail tip, and planning a ring of mane cones swept back around the head for a furry crest effect.
